Isaac's trembling question mi epho ('who then?', Gen 27:33) upon discovering Jacob's deception is its most dramatic occurrence. In Job it punctuates anguished reasoning: 'where then is my hope?' (17:15). The particle also appears in deliberative contexts: 'if it must be so, then do this' (Gen 43:11). German 'also/denn,' Spanish 'entonces/pues,' and French 'alors' each approximate this emphatic-inferential nuance."

Also used in deliberative contexts (Gen 43:11). Functionally parallels Greek ara/pote and Latin tandem.
    Existing Spanish translations: entonces, es-él,, pues
